sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 06-01-2024.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 06-01-2024 at about 3.00 p.m., the petitioner was pedestrian at 3rd cross, 3rd main, new extension, opposite to Moksha Metal, Kalasipalya, Bengaluru City, at that time the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL- 5160 driven the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and the wheels of the said tempo ran over the right foot of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Victoria hospital, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and discharged with an advice of regular followup treatment and bed rest.
The petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment and attendant expenses.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 62 years and was working as Coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, petitioner is still under treatment and lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.1 and 2 being the RC Owner and insurer of the offending tempo is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, respondent No.1 owner has not appeared before the court, hence,
placed as Exparte.
After service of summons, Respondent No.2 - insurance company has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by admitting the issuance of policy to the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.

It has denied the cause and manner of accident by contending that, the petitioner being the pedestrian crossed the road where there is no provision for crossing the road and hence contributed towards the cause of accident.

Further it has contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license at the time of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.

Further contended that, there is no nexus between the accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner and hence the complaint was lodged after the lapse of 1 day from the date of occurrence of accident.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and on higher side.
Hence, this respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following points are framed by this court:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Tempo bearing Reg. NO.KA-05-AL- 5160 by its driver in RTA took place on 06.01.2024 at about 3.00 p.m. at 3 rd cross, 3rd main new extension, Opposite Moksha Metal, Kalasipalya, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum amount & from whom?
3 . What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.
Further examined the Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic surgeon as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.16 & P.17 and closed their side evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

6. Heard the arguments and perused evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final orders  for the following:-

 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as PW.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR and complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, Statement of the petitioner, wound certificate, IMV notice and reply U/Sec.133 of MV Act and charge sheet which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 11.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of the first information given by the son of the petitioner by alleging the negligence of the driver of Tempo.
In continuation, the IO conducted spot mahazar and rough sketch as per Ex.P.3 and P.4.
As per the spot mahazar marked at Ex.P3 and rough sketch at Ex.P.4 the accident spot is in the middle of the road.
As per Ex.P5 no visible damages found on the said offending vehicle.
It is alleged that the driver of the tempo by driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner ran over on the right foot of the petitioner.
Hence, there is no chances of getting the damages on the vehicle.

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that as the petitioner was trying to cross the road where there is no signal and pedestrian crossing the contributory negligence has to be considered.

In this regard if we perused the Ex.P.3 complaint it is alleged while the petitioner was working near a shop as a coolie the offending vehicle came from backside and ran over on the right foot of the petitioner.
As per the spot mahazar also it is found that the said accident spot is of business area where the heavy vehicles expected to be more cautious.
The driver of the tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL- 5160 has drove his vehicle in a market place in rash and negligent manner.
Thus it is the negligence on the part of the driver of the tempo and no grounds are made out to consider the contributory negligence.

11. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by deposing the negligence of the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160 and produced documents in support of his case to prove the alleged negligence.
The respondent No.1 being the owner neither filed written statement nor cross-examined to disprove the case of the petitioner.
12. Ex.P11 charge sheet is also came to be filed on the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
The IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
No grounds are made out by the respondent to show that contributory negligence from the petitioner.

It is very important to note that if the driver of Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL- 5160 was in a controllable speed and if he was not negligent he could have controlled his vehicle in a market place where it is expected to be more crouded.

This shows the gross negligence of the driver of Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
13.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
14.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b), 187 of MV Act.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

By relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.

sentences.text: In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

17. In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 11 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 06-01-2024 which is caused by the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160 which belonging to respondent.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05- AL-5160.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.
a) PAIN AND AGONY:-
Petitioner has alleged that at the time of accident he was aged about 62 years.
As per Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P15 the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 08-07-1961.
The accident took place on 06-01-2024.
Hence as on the date of accident, petitioner was aged about 63 years.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P12 the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at Victoria hospital from 06- 01-2024 to 21.01.2024 for a period of 16 days and sustained right foot crush injury with D1 to D4 proximal phalanx fracture with D5 metatarsal fracture and underwent D1 shortening closure with stay suturing followed by debridement on 11.01.2024.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

5 b) Medical expenses:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P13, amounting to Rs.10,866/-.
These bills are supported by the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills are not seriously disputed by the respondent and no grounds are made out to disbelieving these bills.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.10,900/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period: The petitioner has stated that he was working as coolie and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
In the absence of any document the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.16,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2024.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P12 petitioner was admitted to Victoria Hospital and underwent the operation.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence, this court is of the opinion that in total four months period may be considered under this head as a loss of income.
So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500 X 4 months = Rs.66,000/- during the laid up period.

d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon as PW.2, through him Clinical notes and X-ray are marked at Ex.P16 &
P17.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right foot crush injury with D1 to D4 proximal phalanx fracture with D5 metatarsal fracture and underwent D1 shortening closure with stay suturing followed by debridement on 11.01.2024.
PW.2 has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of right and left lower limb at 38% and to the whole body at 13%.
According to the petitioner he was working as Coolie and suffered with right foot crush injury with D1 to D4 proximal phalanx fracture with D5 metatarsal fracture.
In the complaint itself it is alleged while the petitioner working as a coolie near a shop the said accident was caused.
The disability caused to the petitioner may affect on his occupation to greater extent.
Hence, I hold that the petitioner sustained disability of 10% to the whole body.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '7'.
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.16,500/- X 12 X 7 X 10% =Rs.1,38,600/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE;
As per discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted to Victoria Hospital and took treatment as inpatient and underwent surgery.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P8 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
By considering the nature of injuries and the period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident.
Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

The petitioner admitted to Victoria Hospital as per Ex.P12 and underwent surgery for the fractures Thangaraj M vs Aravind A on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186043684/
6 sustained by him.
There is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the injuries as discussed above, it may be considered to award attendant charges Rs.16,000/- - in total as he was inpatient for a period of 16 days in the hospital as pleaded in the petition.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

h) Towards future medical expenses: NIL a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/-
b) Towards Medical expenses Rs. 10,900/-
c) Loss of income during laid up Rs. 66,000/-
period d) Towards loss of disability Rs. 1,38,600/-
e) Towards food nourishment and Rs. 20,000/-
conveyance f) Towards attendant charges Rs. 16,000/-
g) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
h) Future Medical Expenses NIL  Total Rs.3,21,500/-
20.
Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the Tempo bearing No.KA-05-AL-5160.
No evidence is placed by the respondent No.2 insurance company to eschew their liability.
No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- owner.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.3,21,500/- (Rupees Three lakh twenty one thousand five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of  compensation awarded the entire compensation is ordered to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment on his proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
